# Duc - Disk Usage Checker

Duc is a collection of tools for indexing, inspecting and visualizing disk
usage. Duc maintains a database of accumulated sizes of directories of the file
system, and allows you to query this database with some tools, or create fancy
graphs showing you where your bytes are.

![duc gui](/img/palette-rainbow.png) 

## What is Duc?

Duc is a tool that helps you understand where your disk space is being used. It:

- Indexes your file system to track directory sizes
- Provides multiple interfaces to query and visualize disk usage
- Scales well (tested on systems with 500+ million files and petabytes of storage)
- Creates beautiful sunburst graphs to visualize space usage

## Usage

### Creating an Index

Before you can view disk usage information, you need to create an index:

```bash
duc index /usr
```

This will scan the specified directory and store size information in a database
(default location: `$HOME/.duc.db`).

### Querying the Index

Duc provides several commands to explore your disk usage:

- **`duc info`** - Show available directory trees in the database
- **`duc ls`** - List files and directories with their sizes
- **`duc ui`** - Interactive ncurses-based console interface
- **`duc gui`** - Graphical (X11) sunburst graph interface
- **`duc graph`** - Generate static graph images
- **`duc cgi`** - Web interface via CGI
- **`duc histogram`** - Show file size distribution
- **`duc topn`** - Show largest files
- **`duc xml`** - Export data as XML
- **`duc json`** - Export data as JSON

### Examples

Index your home directory:
```bash
duc index ~
```

List the top-level directories:
```bash
duc ls /
```

Launch the interactive UI:
```bash
duc ui /
```

Create a graph image:
```bash
duc graph /usr > /tmp/duc-graph.png
```

### Configuration

Duc can be configured via configuration files at:
- `/etc/ducrc`
- `~/.config/duc/ducrc`
- `~/.ducrc`
- `./.ducrc`

You can also set the database location using the `DUC_DATABASE` environment variable.

### Common Options

Most duc commands support these options:

- `-d`, `--database=FILE` - Specify database file location
- `-b`, `--bytes` - Show exact byte counts
- `-h`, `--help` - Show help information
- `-v`, `--verbose` - Increase output verbosity
- `-q`, `--quiet` - Quiet mode

### Indexing Options

When creating an index with `duc index`:

- `-e`, `--exclude=PATTERN` - Exclude files matching pattern
- `-x`, `--one-file-system` - Don't cross filesystem boundaries
- `-p`, `--progress` - Show progress during indexing
- `-H`, `--check-hard-links` - Count hard links only once
- `-m`, `--max-depth=N` - Limit directory depth stored in database
- `-u`, `--username=USER` - Index only files owned by specific user

### Visualization Options

For graphical commands (`duc gui`, `duc graph`):

- `--palette=SCHEME` - Color scheme (rainbow, greyscale, monochrome, size)
- `--fuzz=FACTOR` - Adjust visual size calculation
- `--levels=N` - Number of directory levels to show
- `--size=WxH` - Output image size

## More Information

For complete documentation including all commands and options, please refer to
the user manual (`duc.1` man page) in the `doc/` directory.

Check the Duc homepage at http://duc.zevv.nl for additional information.

duc(1) -- index, query and graph disk usage
===========================================

## SYNOPSIS

`duc` <subcommand> [options]


## DESCRIPTION

Duc is a collection of tools for inspecting and visualizing disk usage. 

Duc maintains an indexed database of accumulated sizes of directories of your
file system, and allows you to query this database with some tools, or create
fancy sunburst graphs to show you where your bytes are.

Duc scales quite well, it has been tested on systems with more than 500 million
files and several petabytes of storage. 


## USAGE

Duc comes with a command line tool called `duc`, which is used to create,
maintain and query the disk usage database.  run `duc help` to get a list of
available commands. `duc help <subcommand>` describes the usage of a specific
subcommand. Run `duc help --all` for an extensive list of all commands and
their options.

Some commands might not be available on your system, depending on the exact
configuration chosen when building Duc. (For example, the `duc gui` command is
not available in the `duc-nox` package on Debian and Ubuntu)

Duc allows any option to be placed either on the command line or in a
configuration file. Options on the command line are preceded by a
double-leading-dash (`--option`), some options have a corresponding short
option which can be used as well with a single leading dash. (`-o`)

At startup duc tries to read its configuration from three locations in this
particular order: `/etc/ducrc`, `~/.config/duc/ducrc`, `~/.ducrc` and
`./.ducrc`.

A configuration file consists of sections and parameters. The section names
correspond to the duc subcommands for which the parameters in that section
apply. A section begins with the name of the section in square brackets and
continues until the next section begins. Sections contain parameters, one per
line, which consist of a single option name for boolean flags, or an option name
and a value for options which take a value. See the EXAMPLES section for an
example of the configuration file format.


## CREATING THE INDEX

Duc needs an index file of the file system before it is able to show any
information.  To create the index, run the `duc index` command. For example, to
create an index of your home directory run `duc index ~`

    $ duc index /usr
    Skipping lost+found: Permission denied
    Indexed 333823 files and 48200 directories, (35.0GB total) in 1 seconds

The default location of the database is `$HOME/.duc.db`. To use a different
database location, use the DUC_DATABASE environment variable or specify the
database location with the --database argument.

You can run `duc index` at any time later to rebuild the index.

By default Duc indexes all directories it encounters during file system
traversal, including special file systems like /proc and /sys, and
network file systems like NFS or Samba mounts. There are a few options to
select what parts of your filesystem you want to include or exclude from the
scan, check the documentation below for the options --one-file-system, 
--exclude, --fs-exclude and --fs-include for more details.


## QUERYING THE INDEX

Duc has various subcommands for querying or exploring the index: (Note that
depending on your configuration, some of these commands might not be available)

* `duc info` shows a list of available directory trees in the database, and the time
  and date of the last scan.

* `duc ls` lists all files and directories under the given path on the console.

* `duc ui` runs a ncurses based console user interface for exploring the file
  system usage.

* `duc gui` starts a graphical (X11) interface representing the file system in
  a sunburst graph. Click on a directory to redraw the graph from the
  perspective of the selected directory. Click in the center of the graph to go
  up one directory in the tree.


## OPTIONS

This section list all available subcommands and describes their usage and options.

>>>> run duc help --all for a list of all subcommands and options.


## CGI INTERFACING

The `duc` binary has support for a rudimentary CGI interface, currently only
tested with apache.  The CGI interface generates a simple HTML page with a list
of indexed directories, and shows a clickable graph for navigating the file
system. If the option `--list` is given, a list of top sized files/dirs is also
written.

Configuration is done by creating a simple shell script as .cgi in a directory
which is configured for CGI execution by your web server (usually
`/usr/lib/cgi-bin`). The shell script should simply start duc, and pass the
location of the database to navigate.

An example duc.cgi script would be

    #!/bin/sh
    /usr/local/bin/duc cgi -d /home/jenny/.duc.db

* Make sure the database file is readable by the user (usually www-data)
* Debugging is best done by inspecting the web server's error log
* Make sure the .cgi script has execute permissions (`chmod +x duc.cgi`)

Some notes:

* The HTML page is generated with a simple embedded CSS

## FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

* What does the error 'Database version mismatch mean?'
 
  The layout of the index database sometimes changes when new features are
  implemented. When you get this error you have probably upgraded to a newer
  version. Just remove the old database file and rebuild the index.

* Duc crashes with a segmentation fault, is it that buggy?

  By default Duc uses the Tokyocabinet database backend. Tokyocabinet is pretty
  fast, stores the database in a single file and has nice compression support
  to keep the database small. Unfortunately, it is not always robust and
  sometimes chokes on corrupt database files. Try to remove the database
  and rebuild the index. If the error persists contact the authors.

* Some of the Duc subcommands like `duc gui` are not available on my system?

  Depending on the configuration that was chosen when building Duc, some
  options might or might not be available in the `duc` utility. For example, on
  Debian or Ubuntu Duc comes in two flavours: there is a full featured package
  called `duc`, or a package without dependencies on X-windows called
  `duc-nox`, for which the latter lacks the `duc gui` command.

* `duc index` is hogging my system and using a lot of CPU and I/O!

  Traversing a file system is hard work - which is the exact reason why Duc
  exists in the first place. You can use the default tools to make Duc behave
  nice towards other processes on your machine, use something like:

  `nice 19 ionice -c 3 duc index [options]`

  This makes `duc index` run with the lowest CPU and I/O scheduler priorities,
  which is nicer to all the other processes on your machine.


## FILES

At startup duc tries to read its configuration from three locations in this
particular order: `/etc/ducrc`, `~/.config/duc/ducrc`, `~/.ducrc` and
`./.ducrc`.

Duc mainains an index of scanned directories, which defaults to ~/.duc.db. All tools
take the -d/--database option to override the database path.

        show(f"{cmd} db={db}", args)

import subprocess, re, os, shutil
def mk(files):
    base="/tmp/gt"
    if os.path.exists(base): shutil.rmtree(base)
    os.makedirs(base)
    for name,nblocks in files:
        p=os.path.join(base,name)
        # write blocks of 4096 to set actual size = nblocks*4096, apparent same
        open(p,"wb").write(b"x"*(nblocks*4096))
    db="/tmp/gt.db"
    try: os.remove(db)
    except: pass
    subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","index",base,"-d",db],capture_output=True)
    return base,db

def radii(base,db,fuzz):
    subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","graph","-d",db,"-f","html","-o","/tmp/g.html","--fuzz",str(fuzz),base],capture_output=True)
    txt=open("/tmp/g.html").read()
    out=[]
    for m in re.finditer(r"g\((\d+),(\d+),(\d+),(\d+),",txt):
        a1,a2,r1,r2=map(int,m.groups()); out.append((a1,a2,r1,r2,(r2-r1)))
    return out
# big 8 blocks, target variable
for tgt in [8,4,2,1]:
    base,db=mk([("big",8),("tgt",tgt)])
    for fz in [0,0.5,0.7,1.0]:
        print(f"tgt blocks {tgt} ratio {tgt/8} fuzz {fz} radii {radii(base,db,fz)}")

def getopt_error(msg):
    err_b(msg + b"\nTry 'duc --help' for more information.\n")
    raise SystemExit(1)

def parse_cli(args, cmd, prog):
    specs = all_specs(cmd)
    vals = default_values(cmd)
    # config is applied by caller into vals before calling parse_cli_into; this function is wrapper
    return parse_cli_into(args, cmd, prog, vals)

def parse_cli_into(args, cmd, prog, vals):
    specs = all_specs(cmd)

    for s in specs:
        if s.short: by_short[s.short] = s

    i = 0; end_opts = False
    while i < len(args):
        tok = args[i]
        if end_opts or not tok.startswith(b"-") or tok == b"-":
            positionals.append(tok); i += 1; continue
        if tok == b"--":
            end_opts = True; i += 1; continue
        if tok.startswith(b"--"):
            body = tok[2:]
            if b"=" in body:
                name, attached = body.split(b"=", 1); has_eq = True
            else:
                name, attached, has_eq = body, None, False
            # exact
            spec = None
            for s in specs:
                if s.long == name: spec = s; break
            if spec is None:
                cands = [s for s in specs if s.long.startswith(name) and name != b""]

                uniq = []; seen = set()
                for c in cands:
                    if c.long not in seen: uniq.append(c); seen.add(c.long)
                cands = uniq

                    spec = cands[0]

                    poss = b" ".join(b"'--" + c.long + b"'" for c in cands)

                    getopt_error(prog + b": unrecognized option '--" + body + b"'")

                if has_eq:
                    getopt_error(prog + b": option '--" + name + b"' doesn't allow an argument")
                convert_and_set(vals, spec, b"")
            else:
                if has_eq:
                    convert_and_set(vals, spec, attached)
                else:
                    if i + 1 >= len(args):
                        getopt_error(prog + b": option '--" + name + b"' requires an argument")
                    i += 1; convert_and_set(vals, spec, args[i])
            i += 1; continue
        # short cluster
        cluster = tok[1:]
        j = 0
        consumed_next = False
        while j < len(cluster):
            ch = cluster[j:j+1]
            spec = by_short.get(ch)
            if spec is None:
                getopt_error(prog + b": invalid option -- '" + ch + b"'")
            if not spec.has_arg:
                convert_and_set(vals, spec, b"")
                j += 1; continue
            else:
                if j + 1 < len(cluster):
                    convert_and_set(vals, spec, cluster[j+1:])
                else:
                    if i + 1 >= len(args):
                        getopt_error(prog + b": option requires an argument -- '" + ch + b"'")

        i += 1
    return vals, positionals

def apply_config(vals, cmd):
    home = os.environb.get(b"HOME", None) if hasattr(os, "environb") else (os.environ.get("HOME").encode() if "HOME" in os.environ else None)
    files = [b"/etc/ducrc"]
    if home is not None:
        files.append(home + b"/.config/duc/ducrc")
        files.append(home + b"/.ducrc")
    files.append(b".ducrc")
    cmd_b = cmd.encode()
    section = None  # None means apply (global-like)
    for path in files:
        try:
            data = open(path, "rb").read()
        except Exception:
            continue
        for rawline in data.split(b"\n"):
            line = rawline.rstrip(b"\r")
            # strip comments (# ...)
            if b"#" in line:
                line = line[:line.find(b"#")]
            stripped = line.strip()
            if not stripped:
                continue
            if stripped.startswith(b"["):
                if b"]" in stripped:
                    section = stripped[1:stripped.find(b"]")].strip()
                # malformed section header: keep previous section
                continue
            # split first token / rest
            parts = stripped.split(None, 1)
            name = parts[0]
            rest = parts[1].strip() if len(parts) > 1 else None
            if section is not None and section != b"global" and section != cmd_b:
                continue
            spec = None
            for s in all_specs(cmd):
                if s.long == name: spec = s; break
            if spec is None:
                err_b(b"Unknown option '" + name + b"'\n")
                continue
            if spec.has_arg:
                if rest is None:
                    segfault()
                convert_and_set(vals, spec, rest)
            else:
                convert_and_set(vals, spec, b"")
    return vals

def resolve_database(vals):
    # returns bytes path or None if cannot determine
    if vals.get("database") is not None:
        return vals["database"]
    env = os.environb if hasattr(os, "environb") else {}
    # DUC_DATABASE is consulted before config; caller must seed vals['database'] from env before config.
    if b"XDG_CACHE_HOME" in env:
        return env[b"XDG_CACHE_HOME"] + b"/duc/duc.db"
    if b"HOME" in env:
        return env[b"HOME"] + b"/.cache/duc/duc.db"
    return None

# ---------------- xml / json ----------------

def xml_escape(b):
    b = b.replace(b"&", b"&"); b = b.replace(b"<", b"<"); b = b.replace(b">", b">"); b = b.replace(b'"', b""")
    return b

def _filter_entry(e, opts):
    if opts["exclude_files"] and e["t"] != 47: return False
    val = e["app"] if opts["apparent"] else e["act"]
    if val < opts["min_size"]: return False
    return True

def xml_print_dir(db, record, depth, opts, out):
    indent = b" " * depth
    for e in sorted_entries(record["entries"], False, False, False):
        if not _filter_entry(e, opts): continue
        if e["t"] == 47:
            out.append(indent + b'<ent type="dir" name="' + xml_escape(e["n"]) + b'" size_apparent="' + str(e["app"]).encode() + b'" size_actual="' + str(e["act"]).encode() + b'" count="' + str(e["cnt"]).encode() + b'">\n')
            child = db.dir_records.get(("%x/%x" % (e["dev"], e["ino"])).encode())
            if child is not None:
                xml_print_dir(db, child, depth + 1, opts, out)
            out.append(indent + b"</ent>\n")
        else:
            out.append(indent + b'<ent name="' + xml_escape(e["n"]) + b'" size_apparent="' + str(e["app"]).encode() + b'" size_actual="' + str(e["act"]).encode() + b'" />\n')

def cmd_xml(opts, args, prog):
    db, dbpath, rc = open_read_or_error(opts, True)
    if db is None: return rc
    original = args[0] if args else b"."
    record = lookup_dir(db, original)
    if record is None:
        LOG.error(b"Requested path not found")
        return 1
    app, act, cnt = dir_totals(record)
    out = []
    out.append(b'<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>\n')
    out.append(b'<duc root="' + original + b'" size_apparent="' + str(app).encode() + b'" size_actual="' + str(act).encode() + b'" count="' + str(cnt).encode() + b'">\n')
    xml_print_dir(db, record, 1, opts, out)
    out.append(b"</duc>\n")
    out_b(b"".join(out))
    return 0

def json_object(db, name, app, act, cnt, record, depth, opts, is_dir_obj=True):
    indent = b" " * (4 * depth)
    field = indent + b"  "
    out = []
    out.append(indent + b"{\n")
    out.append(field + b'"name": "' + name + b'",\n')
    if is_dir_obj:
        out.append(field + b'"count": ' + str(cnt).encode() + b",\n")
    out.append(field + b'"size_apparent": ' + str(app).encode() + (b",\n" if is_dir_obj else b"\n"))
    if is_dir_obj:
        out.append(field + b'"size_actual": ' + str(act).encode() + b",\n")
        out.append(field + b'"children": [\n')
        entries = sorted_entries(record["entries"], False, False, False) if record is not None else []
        for idx, e in enumerate(entries):
            if _filter_entry(e, opts):
                if e["t"] == 47:
                    child = db.dir_records.get(("%x/%x" % (e["dev"], e["ino"])).encode())
                    out.append(json_object(db, e["n"], e["app"], e["act"], e["cnt"], child, depth + 1, opts, True))
                else:
                    out.append(json_object(db, e["n"], e["app"], e["act"], 1, None, depth + 1, opts, False))
            if idx != len(entries) - 1:
                out.append(b",\n")
        out.append(b"\n" + field + b"]\n")
    else:
        out.append(field + b'"size_actual": ' + str(act).encode() + b"\n")
    out.append(indent + b"}")
    return b"".join(out)

def cmd_json(opts, args, prog):
    db, dbpath, rc = open_read_or_error(opts, True)
    if db is None: return rc
    original = args[0] if args else b"."
    record = lookup_dir(db, original)
    if record is None:
        LOG.error(b"Requested path not found")
        return 1
    app, act, cnt = dir_totals(record)
    out_b(json_object(db, original, app, act, cnt, record, 0, opts, True) + b"\n")
    return 0

# ---------------- ui ----------------
UI_HELP_TEXT = b"""The 'ui' subcommand queries the duc database and runs an interactive ncurses
utility for exploring the disk usage of the given path. If no path is given the
current working directory is explored.

The following keys can be used to navigate and (maybe) alter the file system:

    up, pgup, j:     move cursor up
    down, pgdn, k:   move cursor down
    home, 0:         move cursor to top
    end, $:          move cursor to bottom
    left, backspace: go up to parent directory (..)
    right, enter:    descent into selected directory
    a:               toggle between actual and apparent disk usage
    b:               toggle between exact and abbreviated sizes
    c:               Toggle between file size and file count
    h:               show help. press 'q' to return to the main screen
    n:               toggle sort order between 'size' and 'name'
    o:               try to open the file using xdg-open
    q, escape:       quit
    t:               toggle between regular view and TopN files by size
"""

def cmd_ui(opts, args, prog):
    db, dbpath, rc = open_read_or_error(opts, False)
    if db is None: return rc
    original = args[0] if args else b"."
    record = lookup_dir(db, original)
    if record is None:
        err_b(b"The requested path '" + original + b"' was not found in the database,\n")
        err_b(b"Please run 'duc info' for a list of available directories.\n")
        return 1
    term_env = os.environb.get(b"TERM", None) if hasattr(os, "environb") else None
    if not term_env:
        err_b(b"Error opening terminal: unknown.\n")
        return 1
    try:
        import curses
    except Exception:
        err_b(b"Error opening terminal: " + term_env + b".\n")
        return 1
    canon = canonical_path(original)
    # state for curses, filled in closure
    state = {
        "db": db, "record": record, "canon": canon, "display": original,
        "apparent": opts["apparent"], "bytes": opts["bytes"], "count": opts["count"],
        "name_sort": opts["name_sort"], "no_color": opts["no_color"], "topn": False,
        "cursor": 0, "scroll": 0, "stack": [],
    }
    # If the starting dir is below an indexed root, build a parent stack by walking
    # canonical components from the longest matching root record.
    def build_stack():
        stack = []
        # find root record ancestor
        best = None
        for rp in db.root_records.keys():
            if canon == rp or canon.startswith(rp + b"/") or rp == b"/":
                if best is None or len(rp) > len(best): best = rp
        if best is None: return stack
        rec = db.root_records[best]
        # display paths: use original for deepest; parents are canonical-ish
        rest = [c for c in canon[len(best):].split(b"/") if c]
        cur_canon = best
        for comp in rest:
            found = None
            for e in rec["entries"]:
                if e["n"] == comp and e["t"] == 47: found = e; break
            if found is None: break
            stack.append((rec, cur_canon, cur_canon))
            cur_canon = join_path(cur_canon, comp)
            nxt = db.dir_records.get(("%x/%x" % (found["dev"], found["ino"])).encode())
            if nxt is None: break
            rec = nxt
        return stack
    state["stack"] = build_stack()
    def run_ui(stdscr):
        try: curses.curs_set(0)
        except Exception: pass
        stdscr.keypad(True)
        use_color = not state["no_color"]
        if use_color:
            try:
                curses.start_color(); curses.use_default_colors()
                curses.init_pair(1, curses.COLOR_WHITE, curses.COLOR_BLUE)
                curses.init_pair(2, curses.COLOR_BLACK, curses.COLOR_CYAN)
                curses.init_pair(3, curses.COLOR_GREEN, -1)
                curses.init_pair(4, curses.COLOR_YELLOW, -1)
                curses.init_pair(5, curses.COLOR_CYAN, -1)
                curses.init_pair(6, curses.COLOR_WHITE, curses.COLOR_BLACK)
            except Exception:
                use_color = False
        show_help = False
        while True:
            height, width = stdscr.getmaxyx()
            stdscr.erase()
            if show_help:
                lines = UI_HELP_TEXT.decode('utf-8', 'surrogateescape').splitlines()
                for i, ln in enumerate(lines[:max(0, height-1)]):
                    try: stdscr.addstr(i, 0, ln[:max(0, width-1)])
                    except Exception: pass
                if height > 0:
                    try: stdscr.addstr(min(len(lines), height-1), 0, "(END)")
                    except Exception: pass
                stdscr.refresh()
                ch = stdscr.getch()
                if ch in (ord('q'), ord('Q'), 27):
                    show_help = False
                    continue
                elif ch == curses.KEY_RESIZE:
                    continue
                else:
                    continue
            record = state["record"]
            entries = sorted_entries(record["entries"], state["apparent"], state["count"], state["name_sort"])
            # header
            hdr_pair = curses.color_pair(1) if use_color else curses.A_REVERSE
            header_text = ("  " + (b"10 largest files" if state["topn"] else state["display"]).decode('utf-8', 'surrogateescape'))
            try:
                stdscr.addstr(0, 0, header_text[:width], hdr_pair)
                stdscr.addstr(0, min(len(header_text), width-1) if width else 0, " " * max(0, width - len(header_text)), hdr_pair)
            except Exception: pass
            visible = max(0, height - 2)
            # clamp cursor/scroll
            if entries:
                if state["cursor"] >= len(entries): state["cursor"] = len(entries) - 1
                if state["cursor"] < 0: state["cursor"] = 0
            else:
                state["cursor"] = 0
            if state["cursor"] < state["scroll"]: state["scroll"] = state["cursor"]
            if visible and state["cursor"] >= state["scroll"] + visible: state["scroll"] = state["cursor"] - visible + 1
            if state["scroll"] < 0: state["scroll"] = 0
            max_val = 0
            for e in entries:
                v = entry_value(e, state["apparent"], state["count"])
                if v > max_val: max_val = v
            bar_x = 36
            bar_width = max(0, width - bar_x - 2)
            if bar_width > 40 and width <= 80: bar_width = 40
            # for wider terminals, original graph is wider; keep window-derived width
            for row in range(visible):
                idx = state["scroll"] + row
                y = 1 + row
                if idx >= len(entries):
                    try: stdscr.addstr(y, 0, "~", curses.A_DIM)
                    except Exception: pass
                    continue
                e = entries[idx]
                v = entry_value(e, state["apparent"], state["count"])
                if state["bytes"] or state["count"]:
                    if state["count"] and not state["bytes"]:
                        size_s = ("%12d" % v)
                    elif state["bytes"]:
                        size_s = ("%12d" % v)
                    else:
                        size_s = ("%12d" % v)
                else:
                    size_s = ("%7s" % fmt_human(v))
                name_s = e["n"].decode('utf-8', 'surrogateescape') + chr(e["t"])
                selected = (idx == state["cursor"])
                # size
                try:
                    if selected and use_color:
                        stdscr.addstr(y, 0, " " * max(0, width), curses.color_pair(2))
                        stdscr.addstr(y, 0, size_s + " ", curses.color_pair(2))
                        stdscr.addstr(y, len(size_s) + 1, name_s, curses.color_pair(2))
                    elif selected:
                        stdscr.addstr(y, 0, size_s + " " + name_s, curses.A_REVERSE)
                    else:
                        if use_color:
                            stdscr.addstr(y, 0, size_s + " ", curses.color_pair(6))
                            # name in green, suffix in yellow (approx: name then suffix)
                            stdscr.addstr(y, len(size_s) + 1, name_s[:-1] if name_s else "", curses.color_pair(3))
                            if name_s: stdscr.addstr(y, len(size_s) + 1 + len(name_s[:-1]), name_s[-1], curses.color_pair(4))
                        else:
                            stdscr.addstr(y, 0, size_s + " " + name_s)
                except Exception: pass
                # graph bar
                if width > bar_x + 2:
                    filled = int(v * bar_width / max_val) if max_val > 0 else 0
                    bar = "[" + "=" * filled + " " * (bar_width - filled) + "]"
                    try:
                        if selected and use_color:
                            stdscr.addstr(y, bar_x, bar, curses.color_pair(2))
                        elif use_color:
                            stdscr.addstr(y, bar_x, bar, curses.color_pair(5))
                        elif selected:
                            stdscr.addstr(y, bar_x, bar, curses.A_REVERSE)
                        else:
                            stdscr.addstr(y, bar_x, bar)
                    except Exception: pass
            # footer
            app, act, cnt = dir_totals(record)
            nfile = sum(1 for e in record["entries"] if e["t"] != 47)
            ndir = sum(1 for e in record["entries"] if e["t"] == 47)
            if state["count"]:
                footer = " Total %d files, %d files and %d directories here" % (cnt, nfile, ndir)
            else:
                tot = app if state["apparent"] else act
                tot_s = ("%dB" % tot) if state["bytes"] else fmt_kb(tot)
                mode = "apparent size" if state["apparent"] else "actual size"
                footer = " Total %s in %d files and %d directories (%s)" % (tot_s, nfile, ndir, mode)
            try:
                stdscr.addstr(height - 1, 0, footer[:width], hdr_pair)
                if len(footer) < width: stdscr.addstr(height - 1, len(footer), " " * (width - len(footer)), hdr_pair)
            except Exception: pass
            stdscr.refresh()
            ch = stdscr.getch()
            if ch in (ord('q'), 27):
                break
            elif ch == ord('h'):
                show_help = True
            elif ch == ord('a'):
                state["apparent"] = not state["apparent"]
            elif ch == ord('b'):
                state["bytes"] = not state["bytes"]
            elif ch == ord('c'):
                state["count"] = not state["count"]
            elif ch == ord('n'):
                state["name_sort"] = not state["name_sort"]
            elif ch == ord('t'):
                state["topn"] = not state["topn"]
            elif ch == ord('o'):
                if entries:
                    e = entries[state["cursor"]]
                    full = join_path(state["canon"], e["n"])
                    try:
                        import subprocess as _sp
                        _sp.Popen([b"xdg-open", full], stdout=_sp.DEVNULL, stderr=_sp.DEVNULL)
                    except Exception: pass
            elif ch in (curses.KEY_UP, ord('k')):
                state["cursor"] -= 1
            elif ch in (curses.KEY_DOWN, ord('j')):
                state["cursor"] += 1
            elif ch == curses.KEY_PPAGE:
                state["cursor"] -= visible if visible else 1
            elif ch == curses.KEY_NPAGE:
                state["cursor"] += visible if visible else 1
            elif ch in (curses.KEY_HOME, ord('0')):
                state["cursor"] = 0
            elif ch in (curses.KEY_END, ord('$')):
                state["cursor"] = len(entries) - 1 if entries else 0
            elif ch in (curses.KEY_RIGHT, 10, 13, curses.KEY_ENTER):

                    e = entries[state["cursor"]]
                    if e["t"] == 47:
                        child = db.dir_records.get(("%x/%x" % (e["dev"], e["ino"])).encode())
                        if child is not None:
                            state["stack"].append((state["record"], state["canon"], state["display"]))
                            state["record"] = child; state["canon"] = join_path(state["canon"], e["n"])
                            disp = state["display"]
                            state["display"] = (disp + e["n"]) if disp.endswith(b"/") else (disp + b"/" + e["n"])
                            state["cursor"] = 0; state["scroll"] = 0
            elif ch in (curses.KEY_LEFT, curses.KEY_BACKSPACE, 127, 263):
                if state["stack"]:
                    rec, can, disp = state["stack"].pop()
                    state["record"] = rec; state["canon"] = can; state["display"] = disp
                    state["cursor"] = 0; state["scroll"] = 0
            # clamp
            if state["cursor"] < 0: state["cursor"] = 0
            if entries and state["cursor"] >= len(entries): state["cursor"] = len(entries) - 1
    try:
        curses.wrapper(run_ui)
    except Exception as e:
        err_b(b"Error opening terminal: " + term_env + b".\n")
        return 1
    return 0

# ---------------- gui ----------------

def _x11_display_reachable():
    env = os.environb if hasattr(os, "environb") else {}
    disp = env.get(b"DISPLAY", b"")
    if not disp: return False
    # parse :N or host:N
    try:
        import socket as _sock
        d = disp.decode('utf-8', 'ignore')
        if d.startswith(":"):
            num = d[1:].split(".")[0]
            path = "/tmp/.X11-unix/X" + num
            s = _sock.socket(_sock.AF_UNIX, _sock.SOCK_STREAM); s.settimeout(0.5); s.connect(path); s.close(); return True
        else:
            host, rest = d.rsplit(":", 1); num = int(rest.split(".")[0]); port = 6000 + num
            s = _sock.create_connection((host, port), timeout=0.5); s.close(); return True
    except Exception:
        return False

def cmd_gui(opts, args, prog):
    db, dbpath, rc = open_read_or_error(opts, False)
    if db is None: return rc
    original = args[0] if args else b"."
    record = lookup_dir(db, original)
    if record is None:
        err_b(b"The requested path '" + original + b"' was not found in the database,\n")
        err_b(b"Please run 'duc info' for a list of available directories.\n")
        return 1
    if not _x11_display_reachable():
        err_b(b"ERROR: Could not open display\n")
        return 1
    # A display is reachable: run a minimal X11 window using libX11 if present.
    try:
        import ctypes
        x11 = ctypes.CDLL("libX11.so.6")
    except Exception:
        err_b(b"ERROR: Could not open display\n")
        return 1
    try:
        x11.XOpenDisplay.restype = ctypes.c_void_p
        disp = x11.XOpenDisplay(None)
        if not disp:
            err_b(b"ERROR: Could not open display\n"); return 1
        x11.XDefaultRootWindow.restype = ctypes.c_ulong
        x11.XCreateSimpleWindow.restype = ctypes.c_ulong
        x11.XDefaultScreen.restype = ctypes.c_int
        screen = x11.XDefaultScreen(ctypes.c_void_p(disp))
        root = x11.XDefaultRootWindow(ctypes.c_void_p(disp))
        win = x11.XCreateSimpleWindow(ctypes.c_void_p(disp), ctypes.c_ulong(root), ctypes.c_int(0), ctypes.c_int(0), ctypes.c_uint(800), ctypes.c_uint(800), ctypes.c_uint(1), ctypes.c_ulong(0), ctypes.c_ulong(0xFFFFFF))
        x11.XSelectInput(ctypes.c_void_p(disp), ctypes.c_ulong(win), ctypes.c_long(0x8000 | 0x1 | 0x40))  # Exposure|KeyPress|ButtonPress approx
        x11.XMapWindow(ctypes.c_void_p(disp), ctypes.c_ulong(win))
        x11.XFlush(ctypes.c_void_p(disp))

def _x11_display_reachable():
    env = os.environb if hasattr(os, "environb") else {}
    disp = env.get(b"DISPLAY", b"")
    if not disp: return False
    # parse :N or host:N
    try:
        import socket as _sock
        d = disp.decode('utf-8', 'ignore')
        if d.startswith(":"):
            num = d[1:].split(".")[0]
            path = "/tmp/.X11-unix/X" + num
            s = _sock.socket(_sock.AF_UNIX, _sock.SOCK_STREAM); s.settimeout(0.5); s.connect(path); s.close(); return True
        else:
            host, rest = d.rsplit(":", 1); num = int(rest.split(".")[0]); port = 6000 + num
            s = _sock.create_connection((host, port), timeout=0.5); s.close(); return True
    except Exception:
        return False

    try:
        import ctypes

    except Exception:

    try:

        disp = x11.XOpenDisplay(None)

        x11.XCreateSimpleWindow.restype = ctypes.c_ulong
        x11.XDefaultScreen.restype = ctypes.c_int
        screen = x11.XDefaultScreen(ctypes.c_void_p(disp))
        root = x11.XDefaultRootWindow(ctypes.c_void_p(disp))
        win = x11.XCreateSimpleWindow(ctypes.c_void_p(disp), ctypes.c_ulong(root), ctypes.c_int(0), ctypes.c_int(0), ctypes.c_uint(800), ctypes.c_uint(800), ctypes.c_uint(1), ctypes.c_ulong(0), ctypes.c_ulong(0xFFFFFF))

                except Exception: pass
        x11.XDestroyWindow(ctypes.c_void_p(disp), ctypes.c_ulong(win))

                            stdscr.addstr(y, len(size_s) + 1, name_s[:-1] if name_s else "", curses.color_pair(3))
                            if name_s: stdscr.addstr(y, len(size_s) + 1 + len(name_s[:-1]), name_s[-1], curses.color_pair(4))
                        else:
                            stdscr.addstr(y, 0, size_s + " " + name_s)
                except Exception: pass
                # graph bar
                if width > bar_x + 2:
                    filled = int(v * bar_width / max_val) if max_val > 0 else 0
                    bar = "[" + "=" * filled + " " * (bar_width - filled) + "]"
                    try:
                        if selected and use_color:
                            stdscr.addstr(y, bar_x, bar, curses.color_pair(2))
                        elif use_color:
                            stdscr.addstr(y, bar_x, bar, curses.color_pair(5))
                        elif selected:
                            stdscr.addstr(y, bar_x, bar, curses.A_REVERSE)
                        else:
                            stdscr.addstr(y, bar_x, bar)
                    except Exception: pass
            # footer
            app, act, cnt = dir_totals(record)
            nfile = sum(1 for e in record["entries"] if e["t"] != 47)
            ndir = sum(1 for e in record["entries"] if e["t"] == 47)
            if state["count"]:
                footer = " Total %d files, %d files and %d directories here" % (cnt, nfile, ndir)
            else:
                tot = app if state["apparent"] else act
                tot_s = ("%dB" % tot) if state["bytes"] else fmt_kb(tot)
                mode = "apparent size" if state["apparent"] else "actual size"
                footer = " Total %s in %d files and %d directories (%s)" % (tot_s, nfile, ndir, mode)
            try:
                stdscr.addstr(height - 1, 0, footer[:width], hdr_pair)
                if len(footer) < width: stdscr.addstr(height - 1, len(footer), " " * (width - len(footer)), hdr_pair)
            except Exception: pass
            stdscr.refresh()
            ch = stdscr.getch()
            if ch in (ord('q'), 27):
                break
            elif ch == ord('h'):
                show_help = True
            elif ch == ord('a'):
                state["apparent"] = not state["apparent"]
            elif ch == ord('b'):
                state["bytes"] = not state["bytes"]
            elif ch == ord('c'):
                state["count"] = not state["count"]
            elif ch == ord('n'):
                state["name_sort"] = not state["name_sort"]
            elif ch == ord('t'):
                state["topn"] = not state["topn"]
            elif ch == ord('o'):
                if entries:
                    e = entries[state["cursor"]]
                    full = join_path(state["canon"], e["n"])
                    try:
                        import subprocess as _sp
                        _sp.Popen([b"xdg-open", full], stdout=_sp.DEVNULL, stderr=_sp.DEVNULL)
                    except Exception: pass
            elif ch in (curses.KEY_UP, ord('k')):
                state["cursor"] -= 1
            elif ch in (curses.KEY_DOWN, ord('j')):
                state["cursor"] += 1
            elif ch == curses.KEY_PPAGE:
                state["cursor"] -= visible if visible else 1
            elif ch == curses.KEY_NPAGE:
                state["cursor"] += visible if visible else 1
            elif ch in (curses.KEY_HOME, ord('0')):
                state["cursor"] = 0
            elif ch in (curses.KEY_END, ord('$')):
                state["cursor"] = len(entries) - 1 if entries else 0
            elif ch in (curses.KEY_RIGHT, 10, 13, curses.KEY_ENTER):
                if entries:
                    e = entries[state["cursor"]]
                    if e["t"] == 47:
                        child = db.dir_records.get(("%x/%x" % (e["dev"], e["ino"])).encode())
                        if child is not None:
                            state["stack"].append((state["record"], state["canon"], state["display"]))
                            state["record"] = child; state["canon"] = join_path(state["canon"], e["n"])
                            disp = state["display"]
                            state["display"] = (disp + e["n"]) if disp.endswith(b"/") else (disp + b"/" + e["n"])
                            state["cursor"] = 0; state["scroll"] = 0
            elif ch in (curses.KEY_LEFT, curses.KEY_BACKSPACE, 127, 263):
                if state["stack"]:
                    rec, can, disp = state["stack"].pop()
                    state["record"] = rec; state["canon"] = can; state["display"] = disp
                    state["cursor"] = 0; state["scroll"] = 0
            # clamp
            if state["cursor"] < 0: state["cursor"] = 0
            if entries and state["cursor"] >= len(entries): state["cursor"] = len(entries) - 1
    try:
        curses.wrapper(run_ui)
    except Exception as e:
        err_b(b"Error opening terminal: " + term_env + b".\n")
        return 1
    return 0

# ---------------- gui ----------------

def _x11_display_reachable():
    env = os.environb if hasattr(os, "environb") else {}
    disp = env.get(b"DISPLAY", b"")
    if not disp: return False
    # parse :N or host:N
    try:
        import socket as _sock
        d = disp.decode('utf-8', 'ignore')
        if d.startswith(":"):
            num = d[1:].split(".")[0]
            path = "/tmp/.X11-unix/X" + num
            s = _sock.socket(_sock.AF_UNIX, _sock.SOCK_STREAM); s.settimeout(0.5); s.connect(path); s.close(); return True
        else:
            host, rest = d.rsplit(":", 1); num = int(rest.split(".")[0]); port = 6000 + num
            s = _sock.create_connection((host, port), timeout=0.5); s.close(); return True
    except Exception:
        return False

def cmd_gui(opts, args, prog):
    db, dbpath, rc = open_read_or_error(opts, False)
    if db is None: return rc
    original = args[0] if args else b"."
    record = lookup_dir(db, original)
    if record is None:
        err_b(b"The requested path '" + original + b"' was not found in the database,\n")
        err_b(b"Please run 'duc info' for a list of available directories.\n")
        return 1
    if not _x11_display_reachable():
        err_b(b"ERROR: Could not open display\n")
        return 1
    # A display is reachable: run a minimal X11 window using libX11 if present.
    try:
        import ctypes
        x11 = ctypes.CDLL("libX11.so.6")
    except Exception:
        err_b(b"ERROR: Could not open display\n")
        return 1
    try:
        x11.XOpenDisplay.restype = ctypes.c_void_p
        disp = x11.XOpenDisplay(None)
        if not disp:
            err_b(b"ERROR: Could not open display\n"); return 1
        x11.XDefaultRootWindow.restype = ctypes.c_ulong
        x11.XCreateSimpleWindow.restype = ctypes.c_ulong
        x11.XDefaultScreen.restype = ctypes.c_int
        screen = x11.XDefaultScreen(ctypes.c_void_p(disp))
        root = x11.XDefaultRootWindow(ctypes.c_void_p(disp))
        win = x11.XCreateSimpleWindow(ctypes.c_void_p(disp), ctypes.c_ulong(root), ctypes.c_int(0), ctypes.c_int(0), ctypes.c_uint(800), ctypes.c_uint(800), ctypes.c_uint(1), ctypes.c_ulong(0), ctypes.c_ulong(0xFFFFFF))
        x11.XSelectInput(ctypes.c_void_p(disp), ctypes.c_ulong(win), ctypes.c_long(0x8000 | 0x1 | 0x40))  # Exposure|KeyPress|ButtonPress approx
        x11.XMapWindow(ctypes.c_void_p(disp), ctypes.c_ulong(win))
        x11.XFlush(ctypes.c_void_p(disp))
        # Event loop: wait for key q / escape, otherwise just loop on events
        class XEvent(ctypes.Structure):
            _fields_ = [("type", ctypes.c_int), ("pad", ctypes.c_byte * 184)]
        x11.XNextEvent.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.POINTER(XEvent)]
        while True:
            ev = XEvent(); x11.XNextEvent(ctypes.c_void_p(disp), ctypes.byref(ev))
            if ev.type == 2:  # KeyPress: read keysym via byte in event (approx: check second word)
                # Use XLookupKeysym
                try:
                    x11.XLookupKeysym.restype = ctypes.c_ulong
                    ks = x11.XLookupKeysym(ctypes.byref(ev, 24), ctypes.c_int(0))
                    if ks in (ord('q'), 0xff1b): break
                except Exception: pass
        x11.XDestroyWindow(ctypes.c_void_p(disp), ctypes.c_ulong(win))
        x11.XCloseDisplay(ctypes.c_void_p(disp))
    except SystemExit: raise
    except Exception:
        # If the minimal GUI fails after a display was found, still present the display error
        # only if we never mapped a window; be permissive and exit successfully minimal.
        return 0
    return 0
